Your first statement is false. Abuse of power is not inherited by giving moderation powers to a select few. If this were true, all of the subverses here would be deleting random comments and imposing ridiculous rules.

Instead, giving moderation powers to a select few makes it possible for abuse to happen. However, even though this is true, most moderators here are not abusing their power.

The wrong thing to do is to continually antagonize moderators and take their power away. Moderators give up their free time to remove the gunk you don't want to see. Why should we impose restrictions on moderators when it'll affect more innocent mods than infringing mods?

The solution, therefore, is to counter the infringing mods, rather than the whole of the mods on the site. One way we are tackling this issue is by imposing public moderation logs to keep them accountable. At its core, the moderation system works. We shouldn't waste resources trying to pick a new house to move to just because the bathroom sink is causing problems.

For your second statement: The admins solve this problem by dividing the workload onto moderators. This works on forums and it works here, too. There will be times when the admins will need to step in, but we need moderators to do most of the job. In reality, there is little difference between moderators and admins. We are all humans, we make mistakes, and, in theory, all of us can abuse power. Doesn't mean we'll all do so.

We have to have mechanisms that allow the community to police it's self while simultaneously not allowing for abuse of sock puppet accounts. We should also consider some way of making secondary accounts more expensive and less disposable.

I believe that we should instead be focusing our efforts onto dealing with bad moderators, which is what Atko is trying to discuss. How to deal with moderators who abuse their power without using a system (like votes) that could be abused by efforts like sock-puppeting. I believe that this is the best option at the moment.
